findings.F1: The check failed on Calmar alone (0.69 against 0.75). Two long falls cause it: −23.7 % over about 500 days from w10, while the coins rose +20 to +23 %, and −17.0 % over 387 days from w21 (2024–2025), while the coins rose +51 %. The case gains in those years were 2018 +0.03 % (t 0.05), 2021 −0.19 % (t −0.32) and 2025 −0.59 % (t −1.66), against +0.57 % to +1.39 % in 2019, 2020 and 2022–2024.
findings.F2: The effect lives in calm markets and is absent in turbulent ones. In the low tercile of a coin's 30-day hourly volatility, the Monday–Tuesday move in Saturday's direction averages +1.04 % (t 5.0, 750 cases). In the middle tercile it is +0.30 % (t 1.28, 747) and in the high tercile −0.04 % (t −0.12, 749). The 5 % worst adverse path over the 48 hours goes from −8.1 % in the low tercile to −19.9 % in the high one.
findings.F3: Low volatility is not an effect of its own. The coins' unsigned 48-hour return on those same Monday bars is only +0.09 % in the low tercile, against +1.04 % when Saturday's sign is followed. It belongs to the brief's own theory: a weekend move made on thin books stands as information when the market is orderly, and is noise when the market is moving violently anyway.
findings.F4: A weekly book that trades only the low-volatility tercile has a Calmar of 1.82 (deepest fall −5.2 %, yearly +9.4 %, weekly Sharpe 1.23). Low and middle terciles together give Calmar 0.97 (deepest fall −13.3 %, yearly +12.9 %). The full book gives Calmar 0.70 (−24.4 %, +17.1 %).
findings.F5: The effect is concentrated in the strongest cases. The top quintile of |forecast| earns +1.63 % per case (t 4.23, 485 cases), while the four lower quintiles earn only +0.07 % to +0.30 % (t 0.19 to 0.98). Trading only the top two quintiles gives Calmar 0.78 against 0.70.
findings.F6: Sunday's move carries much of the information, and it is a separate effect that cannot repair this book. On Mondays where Sunday moved against Saturday, following Saturday earns +0.96 % (t 4.57, 1320 cases), and following it when Sunday agreed earns −0.10 % (t −0.47). Fading the last 24 hours at Monday 00:00, without Saturday's signal, already earns +0.58 % (t 3.81, 2387). At the other weekdays' midnights the same fade earns between −0.33 % and +0.16 %.
findings.F7: Dropping a side does not help. Shorts earn +0.65 % per case (t 2.71) and longs +0.35 % (t 1.85), but a short-only book has a Calmar of only 0.32.

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Saturday is followed over the next two days, Monday and Tuesday, by a move in the same direction that grows with the size of Saturday's move. This holds only while the coin's 30-day volatility of hourly returns is low against its own past year, and the calmer the coin, the larger the continuation.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow Saturday's move into Monday and Tuesday in calm markets only, and stand aside when the coin's recent volatility is high, which is when the book's deep falls occur.
ideas.name: Saturday continuation in calm markets

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Saturday, measured against the coin's usual 30-day move, is followed over the next two days by a move in the same direction. That continuation grows faster than in proportion to Saturday's move, so Saturday's largest moves carry most of it.
ideas.consequence: A trader would put most of the weekly bet on the weekends whose Saturday move was largest in usual moves, and little on the ordinary ones.
ideas.name: large Saturday moves continue
